event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Semis ripped, then reversed; gold and silver bled all week.
SOXX led everything at +9.35% WTD before a -3.67% Friday slide, while SLV -5.85% and GLD -4.58% were the week's funding source. The dominant driver was rotation out of real assets and into a QQQ-led (+3.63%) tape, with breadth healthy (314 advancers, 71% above 50DMA) but Friday's semis reversal the tell.

INDICES — QQQ +3.63% > SPY +2.59% > DIA +2.13% > IWM +1.41%. Large beat small by 1.46pp (large +3.63% vs small +2.17%). VIX closed 19.3, essentially flat vs its 19.4 20-day average — no week-long vol expansion despite Friday's drop. Most notable cross-asset move: UUP +2.01% over 20 days, dollar grinding higher against GLD's 20d -6.95%. QQQ sits BELOW its 200-day MA.

SECTORS — XLE +5.42%, XLI +3.76%, XLC +3.72%, XLK +3.36%, XLF +2.66%, XLP +2.52%, XLV +2.19%, XLU +2.11%, XLY +2.04%, XLRE +0.84%, XLB +0.54%. Top industries: SOXX +9.35%, UNG +8.56%; bottom: TAN -8.62%, MSOS -12.26%. Money went into XLK (+862mm, 98th pctile) and SOXX (+25.4bn, 100th pctile) while XLF (-919mm) and XLC (-882mm) bled. Narrow mega-cap tape.

DRIVERS — Semis and energy led (XLE +5.42% on Brent/WTI strength after reported attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure), with crude-tied FCG +6.55% and nat gas UNG +8.56%. The offset was a hard unwind in metals: SLV -5.85%, GLD -4.58%, silver's 20d now -14.33% with 39.2% ATM IV and a 0.34 PCR suggesting hedging, not capitulation. PPI MoM printed 0.3 vs 0.4 forecast and YoY 6.5 vs 6.6, a mild cooling; no Fed decision occurred. Friday's AMD -8.75% and NVDA -4.22% reversal dragged SOXX off its highs.

WHAT'S NEXT — QQQ's 24.8% ATM IV against SPY's 13.9% is the widest dispersion all year; watch whether Friday's semis fade extends into next week's QQQ maxpain at 680. Retail Sales and Industrial Production both land 11-17 with forecasts of 0.0 and 0.1 — soft prints would test the XLE/XLI cyclical leadership. Polymarket prices 88% odds of a 25bp December hike (+12pp on the week); that repricing is the single biggest tail for rate-sensitive XLRE (+0.84%, the week's laggard) and XLU.
